summary: No new candidate. I read the honest player's restart path: crisium.lua (startup, .removed completion, open_epochs, remove_finished_epochs, pass/idle), prt-epoch.lua (input/seal re-delivery), prt-bridge.lua (observe/update_claims/jobs/attempt/tick after a relaunch), prt-transactions.lua (journal load, pending, submit, forget_settled), prt-supervise.sh, and the stored player in prt.lua (epoch directory layout, commit_epoch_state, seal_epoch_state, store_next_epoch_checkpoint, store_uarch_claim, reopen_epoch_directory, revert_interrupted_input, remove_epoch_leftovers, clear_epoch_directory, remove_epoch_files, stored machine pair and cache, agreed pair), plus machine::store/clone_stored/remove_stored/sync_stored/rename_stored and os::clone_file/write_durable_file for the temporary names they leave. Every stop point I traced ends in a state that reopen recognizes: state.json is the only commit point, everything it names is synced first, leftovers are removed by name (forced) or by the clear_epoch_directory whitelist, re-delivered inputs are checked byte for byte, stored uarch claims are reused, the seal re-stores nothing when its checkpoint exists, and the journal is stored before every publication so a relaunch replaces rather than double-sends. Experiments with fine-grained self-kills (below) found no stop point that breaks the defense. The only problems I saw on this path are already in the campaign: R1-O2-1 and R1-O2-2 (unsynced revert clone chosen by rehash; sealed reopen replaces the synced machine by an unsynced clone and deletes the synced copy), R3-VARO2PLAYER-1 (candidate stored but not broadcast throttles the job), R3-VARO2PLAYER-2 (unsynced parent of epoch directories). Noted but not reported (efficiency, no rule violated, bounded by machine size and --keep-epochs): reopening a sealed epoch whose machine.revert is already gone rehashes the whole machine directory, clones it to machine.revert and fsyncs it, then deletes that clone a few lines later (prt.lua revert_interrupted_input called from reopen_epoch_directory, lines 2864-2880 and 3124-3127).
evidence: Crash injector (scratch: RGRESTART/inj/crashinj.lua, loaded with LUA_INIT_5_4 only into the honest validator crisium) wraps the state-changing calls (cartesi.filesystem write_durable_file/sync_directory/sync_file/clone_file/remove_file/remove_directory/create_directory/rename_file; machine clone_stored/remove_stored/sync_stored/rename_stored/store/destroy/load/send_cmio_response/log_*/collect_*/run/get_proof; prt-rpc publish/simulate) and SIGKILLs the process before or after a random call, a bounded number of times, recording the stack. A copy of prt-demo.lua (RGRESTART/copy, only change: accept a new honest pid after a self-kill) drives the demo through prt-supervise.sh relaunches. Results: smoke seeds 1-4: 19 kills, all 4 runs settle epochs 0-2 with outputs 0-4 preserved; kill points included new_stored_player commit, commit_epoch_state (before/after state.json, during forest tree writes, during stale-file removal), seal_epoch_state (checkpoint store/sync, machine sync), stored pair commit (destroy, remove_stored of the backup, load), input delivery (after send_cmio_response), checkpoint files sync, outputs frontier store, transaction journal store before publication. Story seed 11: 6 kills during epoch 1 (state.json write, forest store, reopen's removal of machine.revert, before eth_sendRawTransaction after the journal store, journal directory sync); epoch 1's dispute (7 adversaries) was accepted with bonds recovered; the run later failed only because the kernel OOM-killed anvil (memory cgroup shared with other agents), which is a harness failure. Logs: RGRESTART/logs/{summary.txt,crash-*.txt,demo-*.log}. All process kills keep the page cache, so these runs test process crashes, not power loss.
not_covered: Power-loss (page cache lost) injection: every experiment was a SIGKILL; power-loss cases were reasoned only (sync ordering of state.json, entries, checkpoints, journal, removals), and the ones that fail are R1-O2-1/R1-O2-2/R3-VARO2PLAYER-2.

Kills inside a C++ call (partway through clone_stored, store, sync_stored, remove_stored, a run or a collection): only before/after each call; partial clones/removals were reasoned (config.json written last, removed last; load fails on a missing backing file, checked with a small experiment).

Restart with the chain advanced substantially while the player is down: the demo orchestrator waits for the honest status before mining, so only adversary transactions advanced the chain during downtime; long downtime (seals of later epochs, settlement, journal candidates mined or dropped while down) was reasoned, not run.

Story mode beyond epoch 1 with kills (epoch 2's dispute, removal of epoch 0 files under kills): the only story run was cut by an OOM kill of anvil; the recipe's own fixed restart points were not re-run.
Kills during a leaf proof (winLeafMatch), during a uarch claim build, and during bisection bundle expansions were not specifically targeted; the random story run hit none of them.
Multiple simultaneous open epochs with a backlog at restart, and --keep-epochs other than 1 or --cleanup=no under kills.
Restart of the forked (non-stored) honest player, the sentinel's own checkpoints, and the vg.lua player.
Restart cost against the clocks with production-size machines (full clear_hash_tree rehash of every reopened epoch machine, clones without reflink).
Windows/macOS persistence paths; filesystems other than XFS with reflink.
